definitions.explanation: Requiring effort or causing inconvenience; a hassle.
The effort of looking after someone or something.

examples.notes: 面倒くさい = bothersome, a pain (colloquial i-adjective form)

examples.japanese: {手続|てつづ}きが{面倒|めんどう}だ。
{説明|せつめい}するのが{面倒|めんどう}だったので、{自分|じぶん}でやった。
examples.english: It was too much trouble to explain, so I did it myself.

examples.notes: 面倒を見る = to look after, take care of

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{面倒|めんどう}は{母|はは}が{見|み}ている。
examples.english: My mother is looking after the children.

examples.japanese: お{面倒|めんどう}をおかけして{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ございません。
examples.english: I'm very sorry for the trouble I've caused you.
examples.notes: 面倒をかける = to cause trouble for someone (polite form)

notes:
USAGE: {面倒|めんどう} can describe troublesome situations or the care given to others.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{面倒|めんどう}な (troublesome - attributive)
・{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}る (to take care of)
・{面倒|めんどう}をかける (to cause trouble for someone)
・{面倒|めんどう}くさい (bothersome, a pain - colloquial i-adjective form)
・お{世話|せわ}になる/お{面倒|めんどう}をおかけする (to trouble someone - polite)

CONTRAST:
・{面倒|めんどう} - troublesome (general)
・{面倒|めんどう}くさい - annoying hassle (casual, emphatic)
・{厄介|やっかい} - troublesome (often for difficult problems)
